influences.name: Husker Du
influences.context: The track also finds Grohl offering a nod to one of his favorite bands, Husker Du, with the lyric, 'I'm a new day rising.'

influences.name: The Surfaris
influences.context: The middle section sounded like 'Wipe Out' [by the Surfaris].

influences.name: Stewart Copeland
influences.context: When I was young, someone played me the Klark Kent record that Stewart Copeland had done. I thought how cool that he could make a record and people can listen to it objectively because it wasn't Stewart Copeland from The Police, it was Klark Kent. That's kind of what I wanted to do.

influences.name: Gil Norton
influences.context: We hired Gil Norton to produce. He'd produced some of our favourite records: Pixies and Echo & The Bunnymen, stuff like that. Gil is awesome in that he fucking wrings you out. He wants every last drop of performance and song. It was intense. I learnt more from that guy than anyone.

influences.name: Tom Petty
influences.context: Inspired by Tom Petty's solo work on She's The One, Grohl considered doing a soundtrack.

influences.name: Naked Raygun
influences.context: Dave Grohl still remembers the first punk show he ever saw: Naked Raygun, in Chicago around 1982, at a little corner bar across from Wrigley Field called The Cubby Bear. 'They knew four chords and the singer was, like, on top of my head, and I was against the stage, and it was life-affirming, because I thought ... "Oh my God! This is what I want to do,"'

influences.name: The Beatles
influences.context: I know how I felt when I listened to a Beatles song. Something about connecting to the music that made me feel great.
